content:
Federal authorities are investigating a fatal shooting in north Laredo that followed an alleged attack on a U.S. Border Patrol agent early Monday morning, according to KGNS.

The incident happened around 2:42 a.m. on Monday, November 2, on Serenity Lane near Mines Road, according to U.S. Customs and Border Protection spokesperson Sara Melendez, as reported by KGNS. One person is dead, and at least one gunshot was fired. Officials have not said who fired, and the identity of the person who died has not been released.

The Texas Department of Public Safety has described the incident as an officer-involved shooting, and the Webb County Medical Examiner's Office is investigating the death. Border Patrol and state troopers secured parts of the surrounding neighborhood after the incident, and a crashed vehicle was reported at the scene, though officials have not said how the vehicle is connected to what happened.

Several key questions remain unanswered, including whether the agent fired a weapon, whether the agent was injured, and whether the person who died is the same person accused of attacking the agent. If a Border Patrol agent discharged a weapon, the FBI would investigate under standard protocol, according to federal reporting on the case.

Update — November 12, 2026

The Texas Rangers are investigating the fatal shooting, Telemundo reported. The report did not say who fired, what started the confrontation, or whether the person who died is the same person accused of attacking the agent. Authorities still have not released the identity of the person who died, and the FBI was not mentioned in the Telemundo report.

title: Fatal Shooting Under Federal Investigation After Alleged Attack on Border Patrol Agent in North Laredo
